Topics in the news

Patrick Stewart in 1999
  • British actor Patrick Stewart (pictured) dies at the age of 86.
  • In baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers defeat the Tampa Bay Rays to win the World Series.
  • At least 69 people are killed in a collision between two high-speed trains in Toledo province, Spain.
  • Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is re-elected President of Brazil.
  • In the Serbian parliamentary election, the Student List wins a majority of seats, defeating former president Aleksandar Vučić and his Serbian Progressive Party.

October 30, 2026 (2026-10-30) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Business and economy

  • Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announces plans to cease operations on 9 November, citing pressure from Russian authorities. (Le Monde)

Law and crime

  • Leongatha mushroom murders
    • The Court of Appeal of Victoria, Australia, rejects Erin Patterson's appeal against her murder convictions and removes her 33-year parole eligibility, effectively imposing life imprisonment without parole for killing three relatives with death cap mushrooms in 2023. (AFP)
  • Cryptocurrency exchange Binance confirms that assets worth US$6.3 billion were stolen, making it the largest cryptocurrency theft in history. (Reuters) (Engadget)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 Italian unrest
      • A general strike and multiple protests are held across Italy. Clashes break out in multiple cities. (Rai News)
October 29, 2026 (2026-10-29) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Haitian conflict, El Salvador–Haiti relations
    • Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti
      • The Salvadoran government deploys 2,000 troops to Haiti in response to the kidnapping of four Salvadoran Gang Suppression Force members that occurred earlier this month. (BBC News)
  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
      • Saudi Arabia launches airstrikes against two residential buildings in Taiz, Yemen, killing 12 civilians and wounding three more. (Xinhua)
  • Russo–Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians
      • 14 people are killed and 14 more are injured in a Russian drone strike on a train station in Dnipro, Ukraine. (The Guardian)

Business and economy

  • AI boom
    • Artificial intelligence industry in Canada
      • Canada's federal government invests up to C$1.6 billion (US$1.1 billion) in Toronto-based artificial intelligence company Cohere, taking an equity stake as part of a C$7 billion (US$5 billion) funding round intended to expand domestic computing infrastructure and AI development. (AFP) (Reuters)
  • Boycott of Russia and Belarus
    • Seychelles-based cryptocurrency exchange KuCoin ends services for customers in Russia and Belarus, citing ongoing sanctions. (The Crypto Times)
  • Christine Lagarde, the president of the European Central Bank, resigns, saying she could not remain neutral on current events. She will step down from office in February 2027, eight months before her term officially ends. (Reuters)
  • American food delivery company DoorDash announces an intent to acquire grocery delivery company Instacart for $17 billion in late 2027. (AP) (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • An oxygen cylinder explodes inside an ambulance parked at a medical facility in Tharparkar, Sindh Province, Pakistan, killing ten people. (AP)
  • Three people are killed and five more injured during the collapse of a hoodoo at Göreme's Open Air Museum in the Nevşehir District, Turkey. It is suspected to be caused by heavy rainfall over the preceding days. (AP)
  • Four people are killed and eleven more are injured after an Italian Air Force Boeing CH-47 Chinook crashes near Brčko, Bosnia and Herzegovina. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Swedish government formation
    • Andreas Norlén, speaker of the Swedish parliament, announces a second vote to elect the next prime minister. He proposes a coalition led by the Center Party's leader, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, alongside the Social Democrats, Greens, Christian Democrats, and the Moderates. (Reuters)
  • 2027 Haitian general election
    • Haiti's Provisional Electoral Council sets the first round of presidential and legislative elections for August 29, 2027, with a second round scheduled for December 5, as the country prepares for its first national elections since 2017. (AFP via RFI)
October 28, 2026 (2026-10-28) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
      • Saudi Arabia launches an airstrike at a market in Al Hazm, Al-Jawf Governorate, Yemen, killing 14 civilians and wounding ten more. (AP) (Xinhua)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • Eight women and children are reported to be injured in a airstrike in Kadugli, South Kordofan, Sudan. (Sudan Tribune)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis, Canada and the 2026 Iran war
    • The Bank of Canada raises its policy interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%, its first increase since July 2023, citing persistent inflation driven partly by higher oil and gasoline prices linked to the Iran war. (AFP)
  • Jio Platforms raises US$3.2 billion in India's largest-ever initial public offering (IPO), attracting about $77 billion in bids and becoming the country's most-subscribed IPO before its stock-market debut in Mumbai. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Toledo train collision
    • At least 69 people are killed and 179 injured during a collision between two high speed trains carrying a total of 544 passengers between Los Yébenes and Urda, in the Province of Toledo, Spain. (Sky News)
  • 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season
    • At least three people are killed as Cyclone Arnab makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh, India. (DNA) (Reuters)
  • A bus transporting local tourists overturns in Sarapiquí, Costa Rica, killing three people and injuring 39 others, including seven seriously. (AM Costa Rica)

International relations

  • Rwanda–United States relations, Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict
    • The United States imposes sanctions on the Rwandan ministry of defence over its role in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, alleging that Rwanda is backing the M23 rebels to fight against Congolese forces. (Reuters)
  • United States embargo against Cuba
    • The United Nations General Assembly adopts a resolution calling for an end to the American embargo against Cuba by 130 votes to 17, with 25 abstentions, the measure's lowest support since 1995. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Attacks on Israeli embassies
    • A youth armed with two knives wounds a police officer outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade, Serbia, before being shot and killed. (Reuters)
  • British far-right activist Tommy Robinson is convicted of harassing two journalists and causing them to fear violence. (BBC News) (RTÉ)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Brazilian general election
    • Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro, following his escape from Brazil and arrival in Florida, United States, after the general election, proclaims himself the "rightful" president-elect of Brazil. (The Guardian) (Reuters)
    • Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva responds by accusing the U.S. government of colluding with Bolsonaro to install him as president. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Israeli legislative election
    • Incumbent prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party-led governing coalition wins a plurality of seats in the Knesset, though no alliance wins a majority, leaving government formation unclear. (CBS News)

Sports

  • 2026 Japan Series
    • In baseball, the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks defeat the Yokohama DeNA BayStars in four games to win their 13th Japan Series championship. (Kyodo News)
  • 2026 World Series
    • In Major League Baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers defeat the Tampa Bay Rays in five games to win their first World Series championship in franchise history. (NBC News)
October 27, 2026 (2026-10-27) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • The Persian Gulf Strait Authority says that vessels belonging to South Korean shipping company Sinokor would face legal action beginning on 1 November. (Reuters)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
        • Three people, including a child, are killed in an Israeli airstrike against a tent in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip. (AFP via Asharq Al-Awsat)
  • War on drugs
    • Colombian conflict
      • A bomb explodes near a bridge in Cúcuta, Colombia, at the border with Venezuela, injuring four police officers. (AP)
    • Operation Southern Spear, United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
      • The United States launches an airstrike against an alleged drug boat in the Pacific Ocean, killing five people. (AP)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church reports that at least 60 Christians have been killed in attacks in Oromia, Ethiopia, over the last week. (Reuters)
  • Nigerian bandit conflict
    • The casualty toll from the massacre by unknown gunmen four days ago in Taraba State, Nigeria, increases to 62 people killed and 52 more wounded. (AP)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • The casualty toll from yesterday's drone strike at a market in Nyala, South Darfur, Sudan, increases to over 100 people killed and 112 more injured. (Reuters)

Arts and culture

  • Eurovision Song Contest 2027
    • Netherlands in the Eurovision Song Contest 2027
      • Netherlands Public Broadcasting (NPO) withdraws the Netherlands from the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest over concerns about Israel's participation, after AVROTROS withdrew in August and NPO failed to find another broadcaster. (AP)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
    • Villa Vie Residences suspends operations of the Odyssey in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, after running out of money amid sharply higher fuel costs, forcing 203 passengers to disembark with seven hours' notice. (AFP)
  • AI bubble
    • China's Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market index, which focuses on science and technology companies, plummets 40% in less than four months. (Reuters)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season
    • Indian authorities order nearly 100,000 people to evacuate parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as Cyclone Arnab approaches, with the India Meteorological Department forecasting landfall as a very severe cyclonic storm. (AFP via RFI)
  • Four people are killed, two are missing and several homes are destroyed during floods in Haiti and the Dominican Republic. (AP)
  • A construction site is hit by a tornado in Kepez, Antalya, Turkey, killing four workers and injuring another. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2025 in climate change
    • The World Meteorological Organization reports that global concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide reached record highs in 2025, with carbon dioxide averaging 426.8 parts per million. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Crime in El Salvador
    • A Salvadoran court issues an order to release former president Antonio Saca from prison after the end of his 10-year sentence for corruption. (La Prensa Gráfica in Spanish)
  • Gaza war protests at Columbia University
    • Algerian-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil returns to Columbia University in New York City, United States, after immigration authorities detained him for more than three months over his role in pro-Palestinian campus protests before a federal judge ordered his release. (AFP)
  • Immigration to Nigeria
    • Nigerian police arrest 34 foreigners, including 16 Cameroonians and 18 Nigeriens, suspected of engaging in "illicit activities" in Benue State. The commissioner opens an investigation into their immigration status. (Daily Trust)
  • Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for the United States, despite orders to surrender his passports to the Federal Police, two days after his defeat in the presidential election runoffs to incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The government subsequently cancels Bolsonaro's passports, while the U.S. grants him and his family visas. (AFP) (Reuters)
  • An Egyptian court orders independent news website Mada Masr to close after convicting editor-in-chief Lina Attalah of operating without a licence. The court also fines her E£3,000,000 (US$53,500) and orders the outlet's equipment confiscated. (DW)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 French fuel protests, 2026 French student protests
    • The French Senate passes a bill that would make people who knowingly participate in violent protest groups jointly liable for up to €10,000 (US$11,118) in damage and allow authorities to seize certain welfare payments. The bill heads to the National Assembly for a vote. (AFP via The Straits Times)
  • 2026 Israeli legislative election
    • Israelis vote to elect the 120 members of the Knesset. (BBC News) (Reuters)
October 26, 2026 (2026-10-26) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war, Yemeni civil war
      • Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
        • Senior officials representing the members of the Mecca Defence Alliance, including Pakistani military chief Asim Munir, Saudi defense minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, and Turkish intelligence director İbrahim Kalın, meet with Iranian leadership, including President Masoud Pezeshkian, in Tehran to discuss efforts to de-escalate the 2026 Iran war and the Yemeni civil war. (Al Jazeera) (France 24)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
        • Israel launches an airstrike against a tent for displaced people in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip, killing four Palestinians, including a child, and wounding many more. (Al Jazeera)
      • The Israel Defense Forces says that they have killed four Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad militants in the Gaza Strip over the weekend. (The Jerusalem Post)
    • Egypt–Saudi Arabia relations, Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
        • Egypt's parliament authorizes President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to provide military support to Saudi Arabia if requested amid Houthi attacks in Saudi territory. (AFP via France 24)
  • Somali Civil War
    • Diplomatic and humanitarian efforts in the Somali Civil War
      • The United Nations (UN) announces it will conclude its support for the Transitional Assistance Mission to support the Somali federal government by October 31. The UN will continue supporting Somalia through other smaller agencies. (AA)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • Twenty-one people are killed and 40 more injured in a drone strike in Nyala, Sudan. (Al Jazeera)
      • More drone strikes by the Rapid Support Forces are reported across power stations in southeast Sudan, cutting power across the region. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Karak church shooting
    • The three gunmen who carried out a mass shooting at a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak Governorate, Jordan, are wounded and arrested after a shootout with security forces at an abandoned building. (BBC News)
    • The Jordanian Armed Forces announces that it has carried out airstrikes against alleged positions of the Islamic State in various areas of Syria's Daraa Governorate and Suwayda Governorate, reporting that the gunmen are linked to the group, claiming the killing of 20 militants. Seven civilians are confirmed killed, including three children and an elderly man. (Al Jazeera) (Internazionale)
    • The Syrian transitional government announces the closure of the Nasib Border Crossing with Jordan, suspending passenger and commercial traffic in both directions, after reporting that the airstrikes were not coordinated. (AA)

Arts and culture

  • Dictionary.com says maxxing has been named its Word of the Year for 2026 following a surge in its use across social media. (BBC News)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026–27 European windstorm season
    • Two people are killed and around 90,000 more are left without electricity after the impact of Storm Boelo in Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland, and northern England. (AA)

Law and crime

  • Brazilian police orders senator Flávio Bolsonaro to surrender his passports after Supreme Federal Court justice Alexandre de Moraes barred him from leaving Brazil, one day after Bolsonaro lost the runoff of the general election to incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. (Firstpost) (SBS News)
  • A Swiss court convicts former Belarusian security officer Yuri Harauski over the 1999 abduction of businessman Anatol Krasouski, later killed, and gives him a two-year suspended sentence. He is acquitted over Yury Zacharanka's enforced disappearance. (Reuters)
  • The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation announces they have arrested nine people involved in Nigerian scam centers, as part of an international operation targeting organised crime in Nigeria, locating $11 million in funds purloined by the scammers. (OCCRP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 Spanish housing protests
      • Protests and riots are held in Bilbao, Spain, after and during a political event hosted by far-right commentator Vito Quiles. At least nine people are arrested. (El Constitucional)

Sports

  • 2026 Ballon d'Or
    • In association football, English player Harry Kane wins the men's Ballon d'Or for the first time, while Spanish player Alexia Putellas receives the women's award for a record-tying third time. (CNN)
October 25, 2026 (2026-10-25) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
      • 2026 Houthi attacks on Saudi airports
        • Saudi-led coalition air defences intercept a Houthi ballistic missile and two drones targeting Riyadh Province as King Khalid International Airport resumes limited operations after a two-week closure caused by earlier Houthi attacks. (AFP via ABS-CBN News)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip
        • Three staff members are killed and eight students are wounded in an Israeli airstrike against the Islamic University of Gaza in Gaza City. Four other Palestinians are also killed in more airstrikes in the Gaza Strip. (AFP via Dawn)
  • Colombian conflict
    • The Colombian government announces that a military operation in El Tambo, Cauca, in the previous days resulted in the killing of ten National Liberation Army's members, including two key leaders. (AP)
  • Islamist insurgency in Niger, Foreign relations of Algeria, Foreign relations of Niger
    • Algeria's parliament approves the deployment of army units to Madama, Niger, to protect energy infrastructure, marking Algeria's first foreign military deployment since 1973. (BBC News)

Business and economy

  • Western Sydney Airport in New South Wales, Australia, commences passenger operations as Greater Sydney's second airport. (The Guardian)

Disasters and accidents

  • Twenty-four people are killed and 24 more are injured after a bus collides with a truck on a highway in Makueni County, Kenya. (AP)
  • Eighty-three people are injured, including seven seriously, in a bus crash in Fogars de Montclús, Catalonia, Spain. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Nigerian health ministry expands contact tracing after confirming an imported Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja, identifying at least 44 contacts while investigating additional people who may have been exposed and strengthening infection-control measures. (AFP via RFI)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Brazilian general election
    • Brazilians vote in the second round of presidential elections between incumbent left-wing president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers' Party and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party. (AP) (Reuters)
    • In a vote of 52% to 48%, Lula defeats Bolsonaro to win re-election for a fourth non-consecutive term. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Bulgarian presidential election
    • Bulgarians vote in the first round of the presidential election. Incumbent Iliana Iotova wins and will face former acting prime minister Andrey Gyurov in a second round due to record low turnout and no candidate having a majority of the vote. (AP via CNN) (Reuters)
  • 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
    • Serbians vote for all seats in the National Assembly in a snap election, amid the student-led protests against the incumbent United Serbia government. (AP)
    • The Student List wins the election with 53% of the vote, with former president Aleksandar Vučić conceding defeat. (RFE/RL) (Reuters)
  • 2027 French presidential election
    • French politician Marine Le Pen, leader of the far-right National Rally party, announces her presidential campaign. (Reuters)
  • Crisis in Venezuela
    • Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado announces she has returned to Venezuela from exile. (CNN)

Sports

  • 2026 NASCAR Cup Series
    • 2026 YellaWood 500
      • In auto racing, American driver Kyle Larson of Hendrick Motorsports wins the YellaWood 500 at the Talladega Superspeedway in Alabama, winning his first NASCAR Cup Series race at the circuit. (ESPN)
  • 2027 Dakar Rally
    • In rally raid, Dakar Rally organizers move the 2027 event from Saudi Arabia due to security concerns regarding the conflict with the Houthis. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 LPGA Tour
    • In golf, Japan's Yuri Yoshida wins her first LPGA Tour title at the BMW Ladies Championship in South Jeolla Province, South Korea, finishing ahead of Australia's Minjee Lee and South Korea's Kim Sei-young. (AFP)
  • International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine
    • The International Weightlifting Federation awards Moscow, Russia, the hosting rights to the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, making it the first IOC-recognised sports federation to grant Russia hosting rights for a world championship since the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. (AFP via The Straits Times)
October 24, 2026 (2026-10-24) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Houthi–Saudi conflict, Yemeni civil war
      • Saudi Arabia launches airstrikes against a residential building and a cement factory in Hamdan district, Yemen, killing ten people and wounding many more. (Tempo)
  • Gaza war
    • 2026 West Bank lockdown
      • The Israeli military raids 15 cities in the occupied West Bank, arresting several Palestinians, forcing over 2,000 from their homes, and destroying a three-storey building in Hebron. (Al Jazeera) (Al Jazeera)
  • Nigerian bandit conflict
    • Unknown gunmen attack a village in Taraba State, Nigeria, killing at least ten people. Locals place the death toll at 20, while Amnesty International claims at least 40. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 Karak church shooting
    • Two people succumb to their injuries sustained the day before during a mass shooting at a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak Governorate, Jordan, bringing the toll to nine killed and 40 injured. (CNN)
  • Unknown gunmen open fire against a group of medics in Bafwasende, Democratic Republic of the Congo, while responding to an Ebola case amid the ongoing emergency, killing a nurse and injuring a health worker. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Pacific typhoon season
    • At least one person is killed and 527 others are injured as Typhoon Champi swept near Taiwan. (DW)
  • Six people are killed and another is injured when a passenger train collides with a minibus in Jewish Autonomous Oblast, Russia. (Reuters)
  • Five people are killed in a fire at the market place of Sorsogon City, Philippines. (PNA)
  • Two people are killed and over 2,000 others are displaced by flooding in Chaco and Corrientes, Argentina. (AA)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Florida A&M University shooting
    • Eleven people, including six children, are injured in a mass shooting at Bragg Memorial Stadium at Florida A&M University in Tallahassee, Florida, United States. (CNN)
  • Catholic Church sex abuse cases in the United States
    • Survivors of sexual abuse by Catholic clergy reach a settlement with the Archdiocese of New York in the United States, which will see the archdiocese paying at least $250,000 to around 1,300 plaintiffs, totaling over $800 million. (DW)
  • Five people are killed and three more are injured in a suspected gang-related mass shooting at a residence in Lavender Hill, Cape Flats, South Africa. (Smile 90.4FM)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 European unrest
    • 2026 French fuel protests
      • The Yellow vests hold a second wave of mass demonstrations across France. About 410,000 people participate and over 1,000 people are arrested. (The Guardian) (France 24)
      • About 110,000 protesters march in Paris, France. (France 24)
      • Rioters in Paris attack police with projectiles, but are dispersed with tear gas and water cannons. A gendarmerie helicopter is deployed to locate remaining rioters. (France 24)
      • Party leader Marine Le Pen holds the National Rally congress in Orléans, France. Protesters, including left-wing politicians, marched in opposition. (CBS) (Euronews)
    • 2026 Italian unrest
      • A new wave of protests is held across Italy. Clashes are reported in Bologna, Turin, Rome and Florence. Protests are also held in Milan, Naples, Padua and Bari. (Rai News)
    • Flamingo Revolution
      • Anti-government protests break out in Tirana, Albania. Various government buildings are attacked. (The Guardian)
    • At least 25,000 people gather in Madrid, Spain, in support of the country's state pension fund amid the general election in November. (Al Jazeera)
    • A student protest in Barcelona, Spain, ends in riots, looting and clashes with the police, resulting in 128 arrests. (Euronews)
  • 2026 British Columbia general election
    • The Conservative Party of British Columbia wins the provincial snap election in Canada, returning to government for the first time in nearly a century and ending nine years of New Democratic Party (NDP) rule. Premier David Eby resigns as NDP leader. (CBC) (Reuters)
  • Thousands of Israelis rally in Hostages Square in Tel Aviv to protest against the government, prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet, and the continuation of the Gaza war. (Al Jazeera)
